# infrawrench_compliance_control (Resource)

The organization's decision about one compliance framework control: whether it applies (and, when it does not, why), who owns it, and free-form notes. These are what the compliance page and every evidence pack show beside the control's evidence.

A control with no stored decision is applicable and unowned, so this resource only needs to exist for controls you want to say something about. Creating it over a control somebody already decided about in the web app adopts and overwrites that decision; `terraform destroy` resets the control to applicable and unowned.

## Example Usage

```terraform
data "infrawrench_members" "lead" {
  email = "platform-lead@example.com"
}

# Change management is owned by one engineer.
resource "infrawrench_compliance_control" "change_management" {
  framework_id  = "soc2"
  control_id    = "CC8.1"
  applicable    = true
  owner_user_id = data.infrawrench_members.lead.members[0].id
  notes         = "Deploys go through pull request checks and change freezes."
}

# Backups are the managed database provider's, out of this organization's
# scope, so the control does not apply. Not applicable needs a justification.
resource "infrawrench_compliance_control" "backups" {
  framework_id  = "iso27001"
  control_id    = "8.13"
  applicable    = false
  justification = "No self-hosted data stores; backups are covered by the database provider's attestation."
  owner_label   = "Security team"
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `applicable` (Boolean) Whether the control applies to the organization. A control marked not applicable reads as `not-applicable` rather than as a gap, and needs a `justification`.
- `control_id` (String) The control's id within the framework, exactly as the compliance page lists it: `CC6.1` for SOC 2, `8.8` for ISO/IEC 27001 Annex A. An id the framework does not cover fails at apply. Changing it replaces the resource.
- `framework_id` (String) The framework the control belongs to. One of `soc2`, `iso27001`. Changing it replaces the resource.

### Optional

- `justification` (String) Why the control does not apply, at most 2000 characters. Required when `applicable` is `false`.
- `notes` (String) Free-form notes shown with the control, at most 2000 characters.
- `owner_label` (String) A team or alias that owns the control when no single member does, at most 200 characters. Conflicts with `owner_user_id`.
- `owner_user_id` (String) The member who owns the control, from the `infrawrench_members` data source. Must be a member when written; one who later leaves shows as a former member rather than leaving the control unowned. Conflicts with `owner_label`.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) `<framework_id>/<control_id>`, which is also the import address.
- `updated_at` (String) When the decision was last written (RFC 3339).

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# A control is addressed by its framework and its id within it, split on the
# first slash: <framework_id>/<control_id>.
terraform import infrawrench_compliance_control.change_management soc2/CC8.1
```
